summary: Verified the 'Return to the app' fix end-to-end. Wrote 12 new integration tests in tests/test_return_url_persistence.py covering the gap E1 flagged (return_url wire-persistence + reuse-path update) plus the callback-with-no-params and regression assertions. All 12 new tests pass. The pre-existing 35 unit tests in tests/test_payment_return_button.py all still pass. Full backend suite: 829 passed, 2 failed, 9 skipped in 189s. Both failures are non-issues: test_analyze_spends_free_credit_and_cache_does_not is the parallel-runner flaky documented by E1 (re-ran alone → passes), and one of my own regression tests was fragile against another module mutating the shared auth_helper user — fixed by clearing billing fields before the assertion. Frontend static review of api.ts and WalletCard.tsx passed: RETURN_URL = '' on web, return_url spread into the /pay/order body on native, AppState 'active' listener present, settling ref guards double-poll, refresh(deviceId) fallback when no order is pending. All Razorpay LIVE payment links created by tests were cancelled (verified 10 links → 200/400 from Razorpay).
action_items: No action required for this fix — return_url plumbing works end-to-end. All 12 new tests pass alongside the 35 existing ones.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/payments.py:613 correctly updates the stored return_url on the reuse path — verified live with two consecutive /pay/order calls yielding the same plink_ id but rewritten return_url. Nothing to change.

safe_return_url pipeline in routes/payments.py:81 → razorpay_pay.result_html:209 degrades cleanly: an https/javascript URL is dropped, the page shows the <button onclick=window.close()> variant, and the rejected URL never appears in HTML — confirmed in test_unsafe_return_url_is_dropped_but_order_succeeds and TestCallbackBodyless.
Frontend api.ts: RETURN_URL correctly gated on Platform.OS === 'web' (line 27) and spread into the POST body only when non-empty (line 350). Web path stays clean.

WalletCard.tsx AppState listener (lines 117-133) correctly claims `settling.current = true` BEFORE awaiting settle(), so the browser-close trigger and the foreground trigger cannot both fire poll for the same order. Also falls back to refresh(deviceId) when no order is pending, which is the balance-refresh-on-foreground behaviour E1 called out. No issues.

success_rate.backend: 99.8% (829/831 passed; 2 known-flaky/order-dependent, both resolved by isolation and my test's own fix)
success_rate.frontend: N/A (static review only, per E1 instruction — no browser automation)

seed_data_creation: None persistent. Test fixture cleans up its own payments docs on module teardown and cancels every Razorpay payment link it created via POST /payment_links/{id}/cancel. Verified: 10 lingering LIVE payment links in DB were cancelled (some already cancelled → 400, others → 200). No payment charges possible.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The new tests use LIVE Razorpay keys; the module teardown cancels every payment link it created. If you re-run test_return_url_persistence.py.py yourself, note it creates up to 4 real (₹0-until-paid) payment links per run — the fixture cancels them, but if the fixture ever crashes mid-run, sweep any stragglers with the snippet used at the end of iteration 26 (find db.payments where status='created' and POST /payment_links/{id}/cancel). Also: the shared auth_helper user is mutated by other tests in parallel runs (billing_phone gets set), so any test asserting contact_required MUST unset those fields first — see test_contact_required_still_raised_without_email_or_phone for the pattern.
rca_of_issue: N/A — this iteration verified a fix that was already implemented. No new bugs. Only fragility uncovered was in my own regression assertion (auth_helper user mutation), which is fixed.
